short: Adds low-frequency power (standard: Pei 2011, Ikeda 2014) and phase-amplitude coupling (new) to imagined-speech ECoG decoding (M06); CFC gain unproven: uncorrected tests, equals power.
position: The paper changes the neural input of an imagined-speech decoder (M06), adding low-frequency power and phase-amplitude coupling (CFC) to broadband high-frequency activity (BHA) [@proix2022imagined]. Low-frequency power is standard: 2 of the 5 earlier intracranial imagined-speech decoders used it (Appendix), one uncited here with beta beating high gamma for covert vowels [@ikeda2014neural]. CFC input is new (0 of 5, Appendix) but unproven: it passed in 12 pairs at the same median balanced accuracy as power, 0.60, under per-participant thresholds without correction across band combinations (Fig. 7). The test partition (M12) is the usual within-participant cross-validation. "Comparable to BHA" rests on imagined BHA passing in 1 pair, so it means above chance in some pairs, not parity with a working decoder.
